subject: Clarify: PII ownership, audit log export, and subprocessor justification for DPA annex
messages:
From: Alice Harrison <alice.harrison@medicahealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: privacy@medicahealth.com
Date: Tue, 7 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions for DPA annex: ownership of PII fields, audit logs, and caching subprocessor

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the draft annex. Our legal/privacy team has a few follow-ups before we can sign off:

1) PII field ownership: can you provide the canonical mapping of which Redwood systems own the source-of-truth for each PII field (e.g., user_email -> authentication service; patient_id -> ingestion API)? We need the mapping in CSV with columns: field_name, owner_service, storage_location, retention_period.

2) Audit log export: we need an extract showing access events for service accounts that perform exports (particularly svc-medica-sync) for the last 90 days. A sample CSV with column headings and a stub is fine for now, but ultimately we will request a full export generation process and proof it can be generated on demand.

3) Subprocessor justification: the DPA annex lists a caching layer and a third-party metrics/telemetry vendor. Please provide the business justification for each subprocessor that will have access to transient or derived PII, their jurisdiction, and whether they have contractual access restrictions and SOC/ISO attestations.

We attached a short QA workbook with the fields we expect populated (Medica_DPA_QA.xlsx). Can you get back to us with the CSV mapping and an audit log stub by EOD Thu, Apr 9? Also confirm whether encryption-at-rest keys for customer data are managed by Redwood or the cloud provider.

Best,
Alice
Alice Harrison
DPO, Medica Health
privacy@medicahealth.com

[Attachment: Medica_DPA_QA.xlsx (xls)]

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Alice Harrison <alice.harrison@medicahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Apr 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions for DPA annex: ownership of PII fields, audit logs, and caching subprocessor

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. We can handle this, and I outlined the plan below so you have a delivery expectation:

- PII field map: Marissa will export a canonical mapping (CSV) and attach a first-pass document by EOD Thu, Apr 9. That will include field_name, owner_service, storage_bucket, retention_period, and access_role.

- Audit log export: security will produce a 90-day stub extract (anonymized rows where appropriate) and docs describing the playbook for a full export. We can provide a sample CSV plus the steps to generate a full export on demand.

- Subprocessor justification: Lauren from Legal will coordinate redlines to the annex and prepare a one-page justification for each subprocessor with attestations we have on file. If Medica requires SOC2 copies, let us know which scope you need and we will provide the most recent reports under NDA if necessary.

Action owners & timeline:
- Marissa Cole: deliver pii_field_map_v1.csv (EOD Thu, Apr 9)
- Security (cc'd): deliver audit_export_90d_stub.csv + export_playbook.md (Thu, Apr 9)
- Lauren Bishop (Legal): prepare dpa_annex_redlines.pdf and subprocessor justification memo (Fri, Apr 10)

Will that work? If you need anything faster, we can prioritize the audit export first.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Director, Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: pii_field_map_v1.csv (csv)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Apr 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions for DPA annex: ownership of PII fields, audit logs, and caching subprocessor

Olga — attaching the initial artifacts per plan. Notes below.

1) Attached: pii_field_map_v1.csv — first-pass. Columns included: field_name, example_values, owner_service, storage_location, retention_days, access_roles. It's populated for the ingestion and serving paths that are in-scope for Medica's use-case.

2) Attached: audit_export_90d_stub.csv — sanitized sample with column headers (timestamp, actor, actor_type, resource, action, ip, outcome). This is a 10-row stub to validate format. Full export is available via our internal export tool but requires approvals; steps are in export_playbook.md.

3) Subprocessor notes: the caching layer (EdgeCache Inc.) is used only for ephemeral model KV caching and does not persist raw PII beyond session TTLs. The telemetry vendor (TelemetryX) collects aggregated usage metrics; they only receive hashed identifiers. Both vendors have contractual data processing clauses; TelemetryX has an annual SOC2 Type II report on file. Lauren — can you confirm the wording we should provide to Medica about TTLs and non-persistence?

I'll hand off to Legal for the formal memo and redlines.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

[Attachments: pii_field_map_v1.csv, audit_export_90d_stub.csv, export_playbook.md]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Alice Harrison <alice.harrison@medicahealth.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Apr 2026 10:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions for DPA annex: ownership of PII fields, audit logs, and caching subprocessor

Hi Alice / team — attaching redlined annex and a proposed one-page subprocessor justification template. Key points:

- Encryption-at-rest: for hosted customers like Medica, encryption keys are managed by the cloud provider (customer data encrypted with provider-managed keys), but Redwood can offer customer-managed keys (BYOK) for Dedicated/Private deployments.

- Caching subprocessor: we will state that EdgeCache Inc. only holds ephemeral session KV data with TTL <= 30 minutes and no durable PII store; access is limited to Redwood service accounts with least privilege.

- Audit log process: we can produce full audit exports on request; we need a signed export request and a member of Medica's security team on the call for verification before delivery. The export_playbook.md attached documents controls and the redaction/anonymization steps.

Please review the attached dpa_annex_redlines.pdf. If Medica can confirm the scope of export (full rows vs. masked), we can schedule the export run next week.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: dpa_annex_redlines.pdf (pdf)]

From: Alice Harrison <alice.harrison@medicahealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions for DPA annex: ownership of PII fields, audit logs, and caching subprocessor

Hi Olga / Lauren — thank you, that all looks good for a first pass. Quick clarifications before we proceed with the export request form:

- For the pii_field_map_v1.csv, please flag which fields are considered sensitive PHI under HIPAA and which are non-sensitive identifiers. A new column "sensitivity_class" would be helpful.

- For the audit export: we will request a masked export first (hashing identifiers) to validate the workflow, then request a full export under tighter controls. Can you confirm an estimated ETA to provide the masked 90-day export (we prefer next Wed, Apr 15 if possible)?

- Please also confirm the jurisdiction of EdgeCache Inc. and TelemetryX (country of incorporation / data processing). We need that for our cross-border annex.

Once we have those items, Medica's legal can proceed with signing the redlined annex. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Alice Harrison
DPO, Medica Health
privacy@medicahealth.com
